reviews.comment: Dr. Hatfield's class was engaging and I actually took away a lot from it. There is a writing assignment due every class and A LOT of reading. To me, she did not seem like a very tough grader- If anything, she probably could grade a little harder. Overall, not a crazy difficult course or an easy A, but an adequately challenging learning experience.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: After handing back paper 2 in class, she stood up and critiqued a whole paper that belonged to a student in that class. She literally went through everything that was wrong with the paper. In front of the whole class. I can only imagine what that student was feeling while she did that. Super inconsiderate. Lost all respect for her after that.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Hatfield really knew what she was talking about. Although she was very knowledgeable, she NEVER turned in grades. The entire semester we had 27 writing assignments and only had grades for about 2-4 of them until the last week of school. So dont take this class if you are looking for immediate feedback. I did learn a lot though.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor, with really great and interesting lectures. but she has so many assignments due each week, and the fact that she gave no remote option during peak COVID was a huge inconvenience.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor and class! At first I was a little nervous when I first started history 481 but Dr. Hatfield gives very clear grading criteria and shows multiple resources you can access to help with your paper. As long as you know how to use primary and secondary sources to support your argument youll do well.

If you need to take a 481, take it with her. She's great and super helpful. This is the second class that I have taken with her. You'll have to work for your grade, but she is willing to help every step fo the way.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Hatfield is a wonderful person. There are no tests and it is a good history class for education majors. There is a daily reading assignment that you must do and will turn in at the end of the semester. There are 2 papers to do for this class (3-4 pages) and she was a pretty tough grader on those. Every class is just discussing the readings.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bright side of this class is that there are no tests! However, every single class day you must come in with questions answered upon your daily readings which can get extremely wearing considering college students have a plethora of other classes to worry about. She is a very tough grader on essays. Another annoying thing is the mandatory attendance
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this prof for a relatively low-level history class that I just needed for hours. I'm a history major and am taking several more difficult classes at the same time and Hatfield grades harder than my capstone course. She also assigns amounts of homework that are way beyond what should be assigned for this type of course. Would not take again.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Hatfield is an amazing woman, truly a wise and smart prof. She loves to talk about the readings, which makes the class more entertaining. The essays are simple, and she gives great feedback on them. Don't hesitate to ask for help or go see her in her office. She truly does care and makes the class fun.

She's a very tough grader and there is a ton of reading and printing off of articles. Each class there is an assignment that you have to bring prepared in case she takes them up. She is an amazing professor and really knows what she is talking about! Completely Recommend!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you are not good at writing papers do not take her! 25 writing assignments and 2 major essays. No exams, curve, or extra credit. TA was the hardest grader. I received failing grades on both essays. Super boring and long lecture and attendance is mandatory because they will take points off of your grade.

If you don't like history I would pass. If you enjoy it in even the slightest manner then continue reading. This is not a hard class but it is definitely heavily based on reading. There are two weekly short answer assignments based on readings with a midterm essay and final essay. I enjoyed the class and the prof, but it took some work to do well.

NO TESTS! However, you have short essays twice a week that count for half your grade and then 2 papers that count for the other half. Don't get behind on your short essays! Also, attendance is mandatory, more than 2 and she starts taking points off.

If you don't like history, this class will be excruciating.  Lectures drag on and attendance is mandatory.  You will have to print 2 course packs, but Copy Corner won't print them due to copyright issues.  There are no tests, just 2 papers.  This class isn't necessarily difficult, but you will work. There is a lot to read and write.

NO memorization tests. Attendance, bi-weekly reading responses, and two 4-page papers are your total grade. She's a very chill person but her lectures are difficult to comprehend as she speaks with a "scholarly" tone. No textbook because she has 2 pdfs with a collection of readings-don't print it and save $50.  No online ppts so go to class.
